Petroleos de Venezuela SA Reports Stable Oil Export Volumes in Latest Trade Data

Petroleos de Venezuela SA, Venezuela’s state-owned oil and gas producer, reported steady oil export volumes for the month of May, according to figures released on Thursday by the country’s Ministry of Petroleum. The company shipped an average of 670,000 barrels per day (bpd), broadly consistent with the previous month’s figures, as the company continued to navigate volatile global energy markets.

Officials at Petroleos de Venezuela SA attributed the sustained volumes to regular operations at the company’s key export terminals and ongoing demand from established trading partners in Asia and the Caribbean. “Our export flows have remained stable, reflecting our commitment to reliable supply and operational discipline,” said Juan Martínez, director of international sales at Petroleos de Venezuela SA, during a media briefing in Caracas.

The figures were in line with expectations set by market analysts, who had anticipated no major fluctuations in Venezuela’s oil shipments for the second quarter of the year. “The data underscores the relatively steady footing of Venezuela’s oil sector this quarter, despite some external market pressures,” said Mariela Torres, an energy analyst at the Caracas-based consultancy Grupo Energia. 

Venezuela’s oil exports have remained a crucial source of foreign currency for the country, and the latest data suggests the sector continues to function within its established parameters. Industry representatives, including the Venezuelan Oil Workers Union, welcomed the stable trade figures, describing them as “a positive sign for both workers and the national economy.”

No significant operational disruptions were reported during the period, and the company has indicated that it expects similar performance in the coming months.
